answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a sonnet as the anchor of the cost.
